source.title: Self-consistent dynamical field theory of kernel evolution in wide neural networks

record.file_problem: None; the supplied text contains the full paper and appendices.
record.tranche_reason: The study reports its own CIFAR classification experiment on CNNs trained with gradient descent and measures training loss and classification error across widths and feature-learning strengths. This bears conceptually on V1, but uses two-class CIFAR, MSE, and does not report training classification error or near-zero error.
record.gate_note: The CIFAR experiment reports loss and test classification error, not training classification error. These results therefore do not establish whether the networks reach near-zero training error. The paper also reports training loss for MLPs and linear networks, but those are not benchmark classification-error results for the listed versions. Cited results from other work are not extracted as rows.
record.test_reason: The study tests a theory of feature and kernel evolution, not any listed claim version. Its CNN results report test MSE and test classification performance, which cannot establish V1's near-zero training classification error. It does not compare spurious-minimum frequencies, residual shortcuts, activation-matched initializations, learning-rate stability thresholds, or batch normalization.
record.authors_conclusion: The record accurately summarizes the CNN findings but omits the paper's main conclusion: a self-consistent dynamical mean field theory describes infinite-width feature learning, agrees with the Tensor Programs process at γ0 = 1, and predicts dynamics across a broader feature-learning range than the tested approximations. The CNN experiments illustrate approximate width invariance at fixed γ0 and faster convergence at larger γ0.
record.recipe_differences: The CIFAR experiment uses MSE on two classes and reports test metrics; it does not use or report the claim's training-classification-error endpoint or the listed full CIFAR-10/CIFAR-100 protocols.
record.method_sensitivity: Width and γ0 are varied. The paper reports faster training at higher γ0; in the depth 7 experiment, final test accuracy is roughly insensitive to γ0.

fits_no_version.finding: CNN test-loss and prediction dynamics largely agree across widths 250 and 500 at fixed γ0. Higher γ0 accelerates convergence; final test accuracy in the depth-7 experiment is roughly insensitive to γ0.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: At fixed feature-learning strength, sufficiently wide CNNs have approximately width-independent prediction dynamics; increasing feature-learning strength can accelerate convergence.

fits_no_version.finding: The theory and MLP experiments show accelerated loss reduction with stronger feature learning, and deep linear analysis derives strict acceleration as γ0 increases. These results do not measure the initialization comparisons or stability-threshold behavior named in V4 and V5.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Feature evolution can accelerate gradient-based learning relative to lazy kernel dynamics.

record.problems: The CIFAR experiment uses only two classes and MSE. The reported classification metric is test classification error/accuracy rather than training classification error, so it cannot resolve the near-zero training-error claim. Figure 5 and Figure 10 provide the classification results as plots without textual numeric values. The checklist states that all runs other than the Figure 1 alignment-width experiment used a single wide network.
record.rows_left_out: No rows omitted. MLP and deep linear network loss dynamics are outside the benchmark classification-error outcome in the versions; comparisons of DMFT approximation methods and results cited from prior studies are excluded.

untested.parts: Near-zero training classification error in CNNs on CIFAR-10/CIFAR-100, including corrupted labels and the stated size, stopping, and regularization comparisons.
Spurious local-minimum frequency in ReLU teacher-student problems and its reduction with extra student neurons.
Training-error degradation with depth and its prevention through identity shortcuts or the specified initialization alternatives.
Activation-matched signal-preserving initialization, resulting training speed and trainable depth, and orthogonal versus Gaussian initialization.
Loss recovery, curvature changes, edge-of-stability dynamics, and divergence relative to learning-rate stability thresholds.
Batch normalization's effects on training speed and learning-rate tolerance, and the Fixup comparison.

record.verdict_notes: Changing γ0 jointly changes output scaling and optimizer learning-rate scaling; faster convergence alone is not evidence about activation-matched initialization or learning rates above a stability limit. The absence of training classification measurements is an untested endpoint, not a challenge to V1. Relevant MLP and linear-network results were already declared in rows_left_out.

versions.untested_parts: The CNN experiment bears on training dynamics across width and feature-learning strength, but reports test classification error rather than training classification error. It does not test CIFAR-10/CIFAR-100 classification error reaching zero, corrupted or random labels, SGD or Adam, or the stated smaller-model, early-stopping and regularization comparisons.

rows.subject: depth 5 (L = 4 hidden) CNNs
rows.operation_detail: Trained on a two-class CIFAR classification task while varying channel count and γ0; reported test classification error over training time.

conditions.value: first two classes of CIFAR (boat vs plane)

rows.value: The text says dynamics are largely independent of rescaling for fixed γ0 and that higher γ0 networks train more rapidly; Figure 5 plots test classification error.
rows.note: Figure 5 displays test classification error, not training classification error. The text gives no numeric values for this metric, so the plotted values are recorded as figure-only.
rows.check: Test classification performance does not measure V1's training classification error. Figure 5 is internally inconsistent: its caption and panel subtitle call the measure classification error, while the vertical axis says Test Accuracy. Preserve that ambiguity rather than treating error as established. The faster-training statement also concerns the experiment generally, rather than a numerical classification-error endpoint.

rows.subject: depth 7 (L = 6 hidden layer) CNN
rows.operation_detail: Repeated the two-class CIFAR CNN experiment across widths and a wider range of γ0; reported test classification accuracy over training time.

conditions.value: training steps on a logarithmic axis

rows.value: Figure 10 plots test classification accuracy; the text says final test accuracy is roughly insensitive to choice of γ0.
rows.note: The result is test accuracy rather than training classification error. No numerical values are stated in the text.
rows.check: Figure 10 measures test classification accuracy, not training classification error. Its width agreement and roughly unchanged final accuracy across γ0 do not establish or contradict V1.

source_check.scope: Only the listed rows, labels and statements were checked; presence is not whole-study approval.
